core_obligations: Reduce to the plus construction (proof lines 3472-3478): the sheafification is the plus construction applied twice, and the plus construction sends an object U to the colimit of the zeroth Cech cohomology of F over the pro-etale coverings of U, so it suffices to show that the plus construction again sends finite disjoint unions to products and that it has the same value as F on an affine weakly contractible W.

The plus construction preserves products over finite disjoint unions (proof lines 3478-3490): for a covering of U = U_1 disjoint union U_2, the restrictions of its pieces give coverings of the U_i and the zeroth Cech cohomology splits as a product, because F sends finite disjoint unions to products (including the empty scheme to the singleton).

Value on W (proof lines 3490-3495): any pro-etale covering of the affine weakly contractible W can be refined by a finite disjoint union decomposition of W, and the value of F on W is the product of its values on the pieces, so the colimit defining the plus construction collapses to F(W), which gives the claim.
proof_roadmap: Replace the sheafification by the plus construction and state what has to be preserved.
Check that the plus construction still turns finite disjoint unions into products.
Use the refinement of coverings of a weakly contractible object to compute its value.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a presheaf of sets on the pro-etale site which sends finite disjoint unions to products, the value of its sheafification on an affine weakly contractible object equals the value of the presheaf (statement lines 3464-3470). The proof (proof lines 3472-3497) works with the plus construction, checks that it still converts finite disjoint unions into products and uses the refinement of pro-etale coverings of a weakly contractible object by finite disjoint unions to compute the value. H2: two verifications with two inputs, written out in full.
